PullRequest.Title: ci: install Playwright WebKit's system packages from main's cached .deb files
PullRequest.Body:
The Linux WebKit browser-unit job (#348731) runs `playwright install --with-deps webkit`, which downloads about 176 apt packages. Since the job started running in the merge queue, 9 of its 19 installs took 4.5 to 10 min on slow `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` mirrors instead of about 30 s. One of them hit the step's 10 min timeout before any test ran, which failed a merge-queue group ([run 44495890689](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44495890689)). The slow installs also make the job outlast the queue's slowest job, so they add queue time.

The other Linux test jobs already avoid the mirrors: `install-linux-packages` installs their packages from `.deb` files that the daily `linux-packages` job of `pr-workspace-images.yml` caches on main for each runner image. This PR uses the same mechanism for WebKit's packages.

## Change

- `install-linux-packages` takes an optional `list` input. `list: webkit` installs `webkit-packages.txt` instead of `packages.txt`, with its own cache key and folder. The default list's key and path are unchanged, so its existing cache entries keep working.
- `webkit-packages.txt` lists Playwright's WebKit system packages for Ubuntu 24.04 (the 60 packages that `playwright install-deps --dry-run webkit` asks for, from the pinned `playwright-core`).
- The daily `linux-packages` job also caches the `.deb` files of that list. As for the default list, it installs them and checks that `apt-get` has none left to install before saving, so it never caches files that don't install. Its timeout goes from 15 to 30 min, as a slow mirror can take over 10 min to download WebKit's packages.
- The WebKit job installs them before `playwright install --with-deps webkit`, which then has nothing left to download. Without a cache entry for the runner's image, or if `dpkg` fails, `apt-get` installs them as before, so the worst case is today's behavior.

## Validation

- **Hit path**, in an `ubuntu:24.04` container with the base packages a runner already has (`python3`, `systemd`, `dbus`, and the default list's GTK and Xvfb packages):
  - The action's download step fetched 290 `.deb` files.
  - `dpkg -i` installed them in one pass with a clean `dpkg --audit`.
  - The save job's check, `apt-get install --simulate`, reported "0 newly installed".
  - `playwright install-deps --dry-run webkit` then reported "All system dependencies are installed."
- **On this PR**, with a temporary commit (now dropped) that ran the WebKit job for pull requests:
  - **Miss path**, [run 44517697129](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44517697129): the default list still restored main's existing entry (22 `.deb` files, same key as before). The `webkit` list had no entry, so `apt-get` installed it as today, and the tests passed.
  - **Save and cached install**, [run 44521334925](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44521334925) attempt 1: a temporary step saved the `webkit` entry the way the daily job does. On a fresh runner it downloaded 208 `.deb` files, installed them with `dpkg`, and passed the "0 newly installed" check. The real step then restored that entry from the cache with no warnings and no apt downloads. `playwright install --with-deps webkit` reported "0 newly installed" and took 7 s, and the tests passed.
- After merge, the next daily or manual run of `pr-workspace-images.yml` saves the WebKit entry. Until then, the job behaves as it does today.

> Authored with Copilot

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every fresh merge-queue WebKit job downloaded the missing system packages and transitive dependencies through the uncached `--with-deps` installer before any WebKit tests could run. This repeats a dependency-closure-sized apt transfer for each eligible merge group, despite the package list and runner image being shared.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Slow apt mirrors delayed the merge-queue test critical path by minutes and could exhaust the install/job timeout before tests ran; the PR reports 9 of 19 installs taking 4.5-10 minutes and one install-step timeout.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: On a matching image/architecture/package-list cache hit, install the missing dependency closure from one restored archive before Playwright runs, leaving Playwright no corresponding .deb files to fetch from apt mirrors. Perform package archive acquisition on the daily/manual producer path instead; retain apt fallback for misses or invalid cached installations.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base-revision line runs `pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps webkit` before browser unit tests. The caller in pr.yml:643 enables this job for selected merge groups, and browser-unit-webkit has a 12-minute job timeout. The added pr-linux-test.yml:413-417 invokes the existing package-cache installer with the new 60-package WebKit list; action.yml:84-91 installs all restored .deb files in one dpkg invocation and returns on success without apt downloads. pr-workspace-images.yml:238-242 produces these archives in the daily/manual job after installing the default packages, matching the consumer's earlier default-package installation. Thus repeated package downloads are replaced by one cache restore per warm WebKit job. The PR description reports slow mirror installs of 4.5-10 minutes and a pre-test timeout; these are reported observations, not measurements performed in this review. Blame resolves the original critical-path install to commit 22d53a1ff6572fcdd77a2f919fff96e1f7741e94.

Scenarios.Scenario: Merge-queue WebKit browser unit tests with a valid package-cache hit
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkout, default system-package setup, dependency installation/transpilation, the newly added WebKit package restore/install, and the existing Playwright install must finish before WebKit tests run. The WebKit job has a 12-minute timeout. Acquiring apt package archives is moved to the daily/manual producer on cache hits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Look up and restore one compressed package archive from the Actions cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical restore per WebKit job, with transferred bytes proportional to the missing dependency closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No WebKit package-cache restore; the existing Playwright --with-deps install obtained missing packages from apt mirrors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New cache transfer/extraction must finish before package installation and tests; it substitutes for apt package downloads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the restored .deb files using one dpkg -i invocation, execute package scripts, and audit the package database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dpkg install for the whole nonempty archive and one audit on a successful hit; filesystem/package-script work scales with the installed dependency closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Playwright's dependency installer performed package installation without this preinstall action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before Playwright and tests. Package unpack/configuration work replaces analogous work formerly performed through apt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing Playwright --with-deps installer and acquire the WebKit browser binary; any remaining system dependencies are handled by that installer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful install command normally, at most three outer attempts on failure. No missing cached system-package payload remains after a complete hit; browser binary acquisition remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command also fetched the missing system-package dependency closure before installing the browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still blocks tests. This PR does not remove all installer or potential apt metadata work, but removes matching missing-package downloads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One WebKit job per selected merge group. The list has 60 requested packages; actual cached .deb cardinality is only the missing dependency closure after the runner image and default package list are accounted for, not 60 independent subprocesses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Installation steps execute sequentially within one job; all cached .deb files are passed to one dpkg invocation. Separate merge groups use separate runners. The existing Playwright installer retries at most three times; test workers start only after setup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Key includes ImageOS, ImageVersion, architecture and package-list hash; restore selects the latest run-suffixed entry through the exact-key prefix. The WebKit directory is separate from the unchanged default directory. Successful installation verifies the embedded key and dpkg audit. Workspace images do not supply WebKit itself.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed workflow conditions, cache key/path, batched dpkg success path, producer ordering and merge-group caller are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cache archive size, transfer speed and apt mirror latency were not measured here. The PR reports successful cached runs; dependency SDK internals are external to the inspected repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced high-confidence performance regression. This path fixes repeated critical-path apt package acquisition; the fixing mechanism and blamed introducer were recorded internally.

Scenarios.Scenario: WebKit setup on cache miss, unidentified runner image, or failed cached installation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added package action falls back to apt update/install before the unchanged Playwright --with-deps command and browser tests can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt a package-cache lookup, possibly transfer an archive that later fails installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical lookup per job with a named image; zero when image metadata is absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: WebKit setup directly used Playwright's dependency installer without a cache lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds lookup/possible failed-archive overhead ahead of apt fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run apt-get update and one batched apt-get install --fix-broken for the WebKit package list, including network acquisition, unpacking and package configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two successful apt subprocesses normally, each bounded by 30 helper attempts on recognized transient errors; package downloads scale with the missing dependency closure, not one apt process per package.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing Playwright --with-deps command acquired these missing system packages itself; no preceding WebKit action fallback ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: System-package acquisition remains on the test critical path for misses. It occurs earlier than the original Playwright installer; retry scheduling differs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the unchanged Playwright dependency/browser installation after the fallback preinstall.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one successful command, at most three attempts. Once fallback succeeds, corresponding package payloads are already installed; browser download and possible installer metadata/validation work remain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command was responsible for both system-package and browser acquisition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still blocks tests; the additional invocation is not an additional full dependency-closure download after successful fallback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One package action per eligible WebKit job; apt resolves the 60 requested roots as one batch plus missing transitive dependencies. A failed cache install adds one attempted batched dpkg installation before fallback.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Commands are sequential. Each apt-retry.sh invocation permits up to 30 attempts for recognized transient errors with five-second sleeps. This retry helper already existed but is newly reached for WebKit fallback. The subsequent existing Playwright command has up to three outer attempts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An absent image key skips restore; a missing entry or invalid key falls back to apt. A dpkg/audit failure also falls back. Consumers never save or negative-cache misses; each fresh runner makes its own lookup. There is no per-test or per-package restore loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lookup, fallback, grouping and retry reachability; external Playwright implementation details are not available to quantify residual apt metadata work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Miss-path lookup and residual installer overhead are not measured; mirror latency and recognized network failures control fallback duration. The unchanged 12-minute job timeout still bounds total execution.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression qualifies. The cold path adds setup/lookup and retry-wrapper work, but does not duplicate successful package payload downloads; no sufficiently evidenced material degradation was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Daily/manual main-branch production of default and WebKit package archives
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The default package download/install/verification/save completes first, then the new WebKit package download/install/verification/save. This job runs only on schedule or workflow_dispatch, not on merge-group or pull-request test paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update apt indexes and download the missing WebKit package dependency closure into its archive directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra successful apt update and one extra successful batched download-only install per daily/manual run, each subject to the helper's bounded retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the default package list was downloaded and cached; each WebKit test runner downloaded its own dependencies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extends the producer job, not the merge-queue test critical path. Producer timeout intentionally increases from 15 to 30 minutes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the downloaded .deb files in one batch, audit dpkg, then simulate apt installation to verify completeness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched dpkg invocation for nonempty archives, one audit and one apt simulation for the added WebKit list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These checks ran only for the default list, not WebKit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before publishing the new archive, avoiding caching unusable package sets.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write missing package archives, clean temporary apt files, package the directory for cache upload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra fixed archive directory per producer run; bytes/files scale with the missing dependency closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the default archive directory was prepared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Necessary producer work off the consumer critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload the verified WebKit archive to the Actions cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional logical cache save per daily/manual producer run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One cache save for the default list only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete to make future cache hits available, but does not gate current merge-queue tests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two fixed package lists per scheduled/manual job instead of one. WebKit has 60 roots, with only dependencies missing after the runner image and default package installation downloaded. The effective .deb count depends on those installed packages.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two list actions run serially on one producer runner. Each list batches download and dpkg installation; apt commands use the existing bounded retry helper. Other workspace-image jobs run separately, and workflow-level workspace-images-${github.ref} concurrency prevents overlapping same-ref workflow execution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Producer intentionally bypasses restore and saves a fresh run-id/run-attempt-suffixed entry. WebKit has a separate list hash and directory. Before saving, dpkg must succeed with a clean audit and apt simulation must report zero newly installed packages. Existing default cache keys and archive paths remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: schedule/manual gating, sequential actions, missing-only download, validation and save are explicit in the inspected workflow/action.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Producer duration and compressed archive size depend on mirrors and runner image contents. Cache retention/eviction is managed externally; no evidence shows the added archive causing harmful eviction.
Scenarios.Verdict: Intentional transfer of repeated consumer downloads to a bounded off-critical-path producer. Additional fixed work and the larger timeout do not establish a reportable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Existing non-WebKit Linux tests, chat-lib builds and dependency-cache jobs using the default package list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Default system packages still install before the existing native builds/tests; the added WebKit action is conditionally excluded from these test jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the default package archive or acquire missing default packages through apt fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same one logical restore per applicable named-image action invocation and same two normal apt commands on fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical default archive path/key, list and restore/fallback behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same prerequisite for downstream builds/tests as before the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install all default cached .deb files with one dpkg invocation and audit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged one batched dpkg installation and audit per successful nonempty cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same installation and auditing commands using the original default directory.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Same nine-package default list and same number of existing action calls; one batched installation per action invocation, with installed dependencies deduplicated by the package manager.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing workflow job parallelism remains unchanged; each action's restore/install/fallback steps are sequential and package-manager operations are batched. No new per-item or per-job WebKit work occurs when the WebKit condition is false.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Empty list input selects the same packages.txt, runner.temp/apt-packages directory and original image/architecture/list-hash key. Existing main cache entries remain usable. Restore, fallback and producer validation behavior are unchanged for this list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct before/after diff comparison preserves the default filename, directory and key hash expression; callers omit the optional list input.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing apt/cache latencies are not measured, but the changed parameterization preserves boundary cardinality and successful cache reuse.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression; default consumers preserve prior expensive-boundary behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. Traced WebKit merge-group eligibility, warm/miss/failed-cache installation, scheduled cache production, unchanged default consumers and apt retry boundaries. No qualifying introduced performance findings. Recorded one high-confidence regression fix with base-line blame provenance. Static review; external action/Playwright internals and runtime durations were not independently measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
